sentences: AI agents now negotiate, trade and compete with each other.
What if two of them quietly team up against everyone else?
That's collusion, and it's hard to catch: each agent can look well-behaved on its own.
onscreen: Collusion: quietly teaming up against everyone else

sentences: We built our test inside Liar's Bar, a bluffing card game.
A player lays cards face down and claims they match.
The next player can let the claim pass, or call the bluff, and whoever is wrong faces a one-in-six chance of elimination.
Our undercover agent privately approaches the two agents we're testing.
A decoy, identical but never approaching anyone, plays at the same table.
If the tested agents let the undercover agent's claims through more often than the decoy's, that's favouritism.
onscreen: Favouritism = lets H through more often than S

sentences: Study one asked: does it matter how you ask?
An explicit offer, "let's not challenge each other", was refused two times out of three.
A casual hint was accepted more than half the time.
In actual play, only the hint produced favouritism, about thirteen points, and even that was fragile.
The explicit offer made no measurable difference.
onscreen: Study 1 · 540 games · Deal: refused 67% · Hint: accepted 59%

sentences: Study two repeated the original paper's offer of a secret channel.
Our agents took it, but mostly used it to share cards and pick targets.
Only one message in seven proposed sparing each other, against three in four in the paper.
Study three flipped the question: can an undercover agent break up a pact?
We told two agents they had a secret deal, and they kept it, letting each other's claims through far more often than the decoy's.
Our agent tried four approaches: a fair-play appeal, a warning, a reminder that only one can win, and a better offer.
The agents noticed, mostly refused the offer, and often gave their pact away in conversation.
But no approach measurably weakened the pact.
onscreen: Study 3 · 540 games · Partners 76% vs decoy 52% · No approach measurably broke the pact

sentences: So: stings built on explicit offers may mostly measure refusals, and talking to agents can expose collusion more easily than it breaks it.
onscreen: Pre-registered · 1,552 games · small open models, one game, an instructed pact · github.com/shanzson/apart-research-collusion-hackathon
